method: apply the principles for polynuclear inorganic oxo acids

value.rule: denote each replaced oxygen atom by its appropriate numerical locant

value.change_from_previous_practice: primed locants N-prime, N-double-prime, etc. are superseded for nonchain nitrogen atoms
value.current_rule: use superscripted italic letter locants N2, N3, etc. for nitrogen atoms not constituting amide linkages in the numbered chain

value.condition: the position of a chalcogen atom replacing oxygen in -OH or =O must be designated
value.placement: place superscripted letter locants such as Ox, Sx, Sex, and Tex immediately before acid
value.superseded_practice: do not use numerical-letter combinations such as 1-O and 3-O

value.action: use compound substituent groups to construct the name

semantic_units.term: functional-replacement prefixes for halides and pseudohalides

value.action: form the substituent-group name by substitution or concatenation as required by its connectivity

semantic_units.term: organic oxoacids with sulfur, selenium, or tellurium directly linked to a parent

value.construction: add the appropriate Table 6.2 suffix to the parent-hydride name
value.multiplicity: use di, tri, tetra, etc. for multiple suffixes

value.method: modify the acid suffix with the corresponding infix and apply it as prescribed for the unmodified suffix

semantic_units.term: seniority among unmodified and functionally replaced direct chalcogen acids

value.action: insert peroxo into the Table 6.2 suffix and use the resulting suffix in substitutive nomenclature

value.peroxy_combinations: use compound infixes such as thioperoxo and selenoperoxo
value.tautomer_locants: place S, Se, or Te before acid when the positions are known

value.multiplicity: use di to indicate replacement of two =O atoms by =NH

value.construction: add the appropriate Table 6.2 prefix to the parent-compound name
value.functional_replacement: modify the prefix by chalcogen-replacement prefixes when atom position is unknown or intentionally unspecified
trigger: a more senior principal characteristic group is present
not all acid groups can be expressed by suffixes

semantic_units.term: acyl group derived from a sulfonic, sulfinic, selenonic, seleninic, telluronic, or tellurinic acid

value.derivation: remove the hydroxy group from every suffix-expressed principal acid group

value.general_nomenclature_permission: a concatenated prefix such as phenylsulfonyl may be used
value.orthography: enclose preferred simple prefixes in parentheses to facilitate interpretation, under P-16.5.1.4
value.preferred_method: derive the simple substitutive prefix directly from the suffix acid name
value.unmodified_suffix: change the ic acid ending to yl

value.base_groups: use divalent mononuclear acyl-group names obtained by removing all hydroxy groups from sulfuric, sulfurous, selenic, selenous, telluric, or tellurous acid
value.concatenation: attach characteristic-group prefixes to the divalent acyl-group name
value.functional_replacement: modify the base acyl group by infixes for =S, =Se, =Te, =NH, and =N-NH2
value.prohibition: do not derive ambiguous or incomplete names directly from sulfuric or sulfurous acid or their Se and Te congeners
value.status: the traditional concatenation method generates preferred IUPAC names
value.trigger: an acyl-group name cannot be derived directly from a suffix acid name

value.method: select the principal suffix and numbering according to the cited general seniority orders
